name: Mauritania
snapshot: A Saharan republic that has stayed stable while its Sahel neighbours fell to coups and jihadists, now preparing to export offshore gas.
culture: Mauritania bridges the Arab Maghreb and Black Africa. Hassaniya Arabic is spoken by the Moorish majority, while Pulaar, Soninke and Wolof are spoken in the south. Nomadic traditions, tea poured from a height in three rounds, and poetry are central to Moorish culture. The old caravan towns of Chinguetti and Ouadane hold ancient Islamic libraries.
society: Slavery was officially abolished only in 1981 and criminalised in 2007, and descendants of enslaved people, the Haratin, still face discrimination. Iron ore, gold and fish are key exports, and the Greater Tortue gas field shared with Senegal began production in 2025. The country has become a key partner for Europe on migration.
situation: Mohamed Ould Ghazouani, a former general, won a second term in 2024. Mauritania has avoided the jihadist attacks and coups that hit Mali and Burkina Faso, credited partly to a mix of military reforms and dialogue with former militants. It signed a migration partnership with the EU in 2024 as Atlantic crossings to the Canary Islands surged.
power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected for five years, at most two terms, and appoints the prime minister; the army has been the decisive force in politics since independence, and Ghazouani is a former general.
